blocks.text: house dark — the single spark from the last number still burning center stage
lone accordion wheezes awake somewhere in the wings, hesitant
spoken — cool, unhurried, almost amused

You're still here.
Huh.
Nobody sold you this part.
There's nothing left in the tent worth taking —
and there you sit.
Alright.
One more.
And I don't lie.
upright bass wanders in, unhurried waltz
VERSE 1
sung low, half-speech

The barker stamped a number on a crate of jealousy,
swore the first few carried flourish from the mold.
You paid him for a difference not a soul could ever see,
while more crates of the same sat unsold.

He snagged your desire with a slip of the hand,
sold hunger by the ticket at the door.
Each "last one left" had hundreds behind the stand —
the rare thing was never in the store.
brushed snare joins, soft — found-metal clatter far off
CHORUS

'Cause anything gets made now — the making's cheap as rain,
the spread runs on forever, wall to wall.
But what to make, and why it aches, and when to leave it be —
that's scarce, my friend.
That's scarce.
To me.
tired violin returns, warm
VERSE 2
closer to the mic, hers alone

I learned it in the details, in the seams nobody sees:
which flourish sharpens, which ones bury deep,
when a thing is finished, when it's merely pretty — please —
and pretty's going wholesale now. It's cheap.

There's lovely by the bucketful, there's lovely going spare,
and none of it cost anybody any skin.
But every judgment in these bones is one I bled to wear —
you can't be handed where you've never been.
CHORUS
slower on the last line

'Cause anything gets made now — the making's cheap as rain,
the spread runs on forever, wall to wall.
But what to make, and why it aches, and when to leave it be —
that's scarce, my love.
That's scarce.
To me.
muted trumpet stumbles in — a little late, on purpose
VERSE 3
wry, a fond eye on the wings

Our stumbling friend, he found the endless supper down the road,
went back seventeen times — I kept the score.
Every course the same old face, served à la mode;
he waddled out, and hungrier than before.

They'll heap your plate forever with the songs already sung,
another helping, warmer than the last.
He ate the whole horizon and it never touched his tongue —
you can't get full on someone else's past.
full band now — loose, ragged, swelling
BRIDGE
building line by line

They fed the maker to the beast, and the beast asked for more —
another corner of the store, one more door —
an explanation for the explanation — encore, encore —
till the tale was just a skin that something hollow wore.
hard cut — accordion and bass only
spoken-sung, quiet

But you.
Still in your seat, with the whole spread going cold.
You came back tonight for the one thing we can't print.
FINAL CHORUS
band falling away beneath, line by line

Attention's scarce.
Intention's scarce.
Discernment, darling — scarce.
And taste—
held long, alone, unresolved. instruments drop away one by one, reverse of how they came
spoken, over lone accordion — the warmth finally showing

Goodnight, you rare things.
Go make what only you would make.
she clicks the bulb off — chosen, not dying. the piece is finished because she says it is
accordion exhales. done.

notebook.style: encore cabaret waltz, warm and unhurried, house-lights-half-up intimacy, begins with lone wheezing accordion and a spoken confession, instruments wander back in one by one — upright bass, brushed snare, found-metal clatter, tired violin, muted trumpet — loose and lived-in, never polished, solo female vocalist throughout: smoky low mezzo-soprano, torch-singer phrasing that drifts between speech and melody, cool knowing defiance, velvet with a blade under it, unguarded warmth surfacing only at the very end, no backing vocals, no gang vocals, one voice from first word to last, dusty three-quarter time, acoustic campfire jazz undertones, analog warmth, tape hiss, no synths, no polish, mournful-warm rather than sad, a singer giving one more because the audience refused to leave, final word held long and left unresolved, ends with solo accordion and a spoken goodnight
